step: 1. Confirm beneficial owner and SAFE customer classification
required: Confirm the account owner's identity, whether SAFE/bank classifies the holder as a domestic individual or overseas individual, account type, and any permanent-residence status. U.S. citizenship alone is not enough to select the route.
why: Rules differ for foreign-exchange purchase and outward remittance depending on individual/account classification.

step: 2. Establish the source and original currency of the balance
required: Collect bank statements showing whether the balance is RMB or foreign currency, how it arrived, dates, and whether it came from wages, business, sale proceeds, inheritance/gift, investment, dividends, or savings.
why: The conversion path depends on whether the amount is current-account income, existing foreign currency, capital proceeds, or another category.

sources.label: SAFE individual FX rules and authenticity review

step: 3. Ask the bank for its written path and document list
required: Ask the account bank's FX/compliance desk whether it can convert and transfer to the owner's U.S. account; which genuine purpose category applies; which original documents and translations are required; and whether the transfer can be made in one transaction.
why: Above the ID-only facilitation threshold, banks authenticate transaction evidence. Account-specific approval and current processing are not established by general SAFE publications.

step: 4. Keep source-document evidence tied to the true transaction
required: Examples where relevant: salary/employment and tax records; lease, tuition or hospital bills; inheritance or notarized gift documents; actual trade contracts/customs/e-commerce records; company profit resolution, audit and tax records; investment registration and disposal records.
why: The source category and payment purpose must be genuine; no false invoices, nominee transactions, or quota splitting.

sources.label: SAFE individual FX rules: employment, donations, inheritance, investment proceeds, and remittances

step: 5. Obtain an all-in bank quote before authorizing conversion
required: Obtain the execution CNY/USD quote, the bank's stated spread/markup, sender wire fee, correspondent/intermediary fee assumptions and receiving-bank fee; confirm who pays each fee and amount delivered in USD.
why: No bank, recipient institution or executable quote was provided, so all actual prices are blank/unverified.

sources.label: SAFE policy context (not a price schedule)

step: 6. Separate China tax from FX controls and bank charges
required: Have a tax professional classify the original income/asset transaction and check China residence, any China tax paid/owed, and supporting returns or tax vouchers. Do not label the SAFE quota or FX spread as tax.
why: Chinese income-tax liability depends on the category, source, residence, deductions/exemptions and records; conversion alone is not shown by the cited sources to trigger a blanket tax.

sources.label: China Individual Income Tax Law (official English translation)

step: 7. Review U.S. income tax and foreign account filings
required: Reconcile any foreign wages, interest, dividends, business income, asset sale proceeds and foreign tax paid with U.S. tax returns; test FBAR and Form 8938 separately for each applicable tax year.
why: U.S. citizens generally report worldwide income; FBAR and Form 8938 are information reports separate from tax liability and have different rules.

required: Save the bank's conversion advice, FX quote, remittance application, beneficiary receipt, source documents, tax vouchers, and both account statements.
why: Records support bank source/purpose review, U.S. income and currency-basis analysis, and FBAR reporting.
